newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil shrs stretch losses in thin, volatile trade.
newsitem.headline: Brazil shrs stretch losses in thin, volatile trade.

text.p: Brazilian stocks were 1.3 percent lower in late afternoon trade after seesawing earlier, weighed down by selling on Wall Street, brokers said.
The Bovespa index of the 47 most active shares was down at 11,030 points at 1600 local time/1900 GMT, just one hour before the market's close.
Turnover was 510.8 million reais ($472 million), well below the market's recent daily average of over one billion reais.
"Liquidity is low and that helps the sell-off," a senior trader said.
Shares opened higher Monday, but the market was trendless for most of the session before extending losses late in the day.
Some traders also attributed the market's weakness to fresh comments by word-slinger Communications Minister Sergio Motta.

In an interview published in weekly magazine Veja Sunday, Motta said he was "disappointed" that recent cabinet appointments of two members of the Brazilian Democratic Movement Party (PMDB) had not led to more support from the party for the government.
He also criticized the performance of the president of Brazil's state-run postal service who was nominated by the Brazilian Progressive Party (PPB), another government-allied party.
"In an already weak market like this, anything can depress prices. It is easier now to pressure shares lower, especially because there are not many players around," another trader said.
Last week, amid devaluation fears, Motta helped accelerate the bolsa's plunge by criticizing Central Bank Foreign Affairs director Gustavo Franco.
Bellwether Telebras preferred was 1.79 percent lower at 137.50 reais an hour before the market's close.
Federal power holding Eletrobras preferred was up 0.38 percent at 535 reais.
